people.hannah.relations: Wife of Elkanah. Mother of Samuel, then of three more sons and two daughters.
people.hannah.meaning: She has no children, and Peninnah provokes her each year at Shiloh. She weeps, prays, and vows to give a son to the LORD. Samuel is born, and she brings him to Eli once he is weaned. Then she prays a song of praise.
people.peninnah.relations: Elkanah’s wife beside Hannah. She has sons and daughters.
people.peninnah.meaning: She has children, and Hannah has none. Year after year she provokes Hannah on the trip to Shiloh. Hannah weeps and does not eat. The book does not name Peninnah after chapter 1.
people.elkanah.role: Husband who takes his family to Shiloh
people.elkanah.meaning: He takes his family to Shiloh each year to worship and sacrifice. He gives Hannah a double portion and asks why she weeps. He agrees that she may keep Samuel home until he is weaned. Eli blesses him and Hannah in chapter 2.
people.samuel.meaning: As a boy he hears the LORD call and tells Eli the hard message. He judges Israel, prays at Mizpah, and warns the people about a king. He anoints Saul, later tells him the LORD has rejected him, and anoints David. He dies in chapter 25, yet Saul asks for him at Endor.
people.eli.relations: Father of Hophni and Phinehas. He raises the boy Samuel at Shiloh.
people.eli.meaning: He thinks Hannah is drunk, then blesses her prayer. He scolds his sons but does not stop them. He teaches Samuel how to answer the LORD’s call. He falls and dies when he hears the ark is taken.
people.hophni.role: Eli’s son and priest at Shiloh
people.hophni.meaning: He and Phinehas have their servant take meat from offerings by force. They sleep with the women who serve at the Tent of Meeting. They do not listen to Eli. Both die on the day the Philistines take the ark.
people.phinehas-eli.relations: Son of Eli and brother of Hophni. Father of Ichabod. Chapter 14 names Ahitub as Ichabod’s brother.
people.phinehas-eli.meaning: He is not Aaron’s grandson of the same name. He and Hophni take offerings by force and do not listen to Eli. Both die on the day the ark is taken. His wife gives birth that day and dies.
people.man-of-god.relations: He speaks to Eli about Eli’s house and its priests.
people.man-of-god.meaning: He comes to Eli with a message from the LORD. He says Eli honors his sons above the LORD. He says Hophni and Phinehas will die in one day as a sign. He says the LORD will raise up a faithful priest.
people.ichabod.role: Child born the day the ark is taken
people.ichabod.relations: Son of Phinehas and his unnamed wife. Grandson of Eli.
people.ichabod.meaning: He is born as his mother hears that the ark is taken. She names him Ichabod and says, “The glory has departed from Israel!” She dies about that time. Chapter 14 names him only as the brother of Ahitub.
people.ichabod-mother.role: Unnamed woman who dies after giving birth
people.ichabod-mother.meaning: She hears that the ark is taken and that Eli and Phinehas are dead. Her pains come, and she gives birth to a son. She names him Ichabod and says the glory has departed from Israel. She dies about that time.
people.joshua-beth-shemesh.role: Man of Beth Shemesh who owns the field
people.joshua-beth-shemesh.relations: The cart with the ark stops in his field.
people.joshua-beth-shemesh.meaning: He is not the Joshua who followed Moses. The cart with the ark stops in his field by a great stone. The people offer the cows there. The text tells nothing more about him.
people.abinadab-ark.role: Man whose house keeps the ark
people.abinadab-ark.relations: Father of Eleazar, who is set apart to keep the ark.
people.abinadab-ark.meaning: The men of Kiriath Jearim bring the ark to his house on the hill. They set apart his son Eleazar to keep it. The ark stays twenty years. He is not David’s brother or Saul’s son of the same name.
people.eleazar-ark.role: Man set apart to keep the ark
people.eleazar-ark.meaning: He is not Aaron’s son Eleazar. The men of Kiriath Jearim set him apart to keep the ark. The ark stays in his father’s house on the hill. The text says nothing more about him.
people.joel-samuel.role: Samuel’s son, a judge who takes bribes
people.joel-samuel.meaning: Samuel makes him a judge in Beersheba with his brother Abijah. The two take bribes and twist justice. The elders point to them when they ask Samuel for a king.
people.abijah-samuel.role: Samuel’s son, a judge who takes bribes
people.abijah-samuel.meaning: Samuel makes him a judge in Beersheba with his brother Joel. The two take bribes and twist justice. The elders point to them when they ask for a king. He is not a king or priest named Abijah.
people.saul.meaning: Samuel anoints him, and he rescues Jabesh Gilead. He offers at Gilgal and spares Agag, and Samuel says the LORD rejects him. He hunts David and has the priests of Nob killed. He falls on his sword at Mount Gilboa.
people.kish.relations: A man of Benjamin, son of Abiel. Father of Saul.
people.kish.meaning: His donkeys are lost, and he sends Saul and a servant to find them. The search brings Saul to Samuel. Samuel says Kish has stopped caring about the donkeys and worries for Saul.
people.saul-servant.role: Unnamed servant who says to ask the seer
people.saul-servant.relations: He goes with Saul to look for Kish’s donkeys.
people.saul-servant.meaning: He and Saul search for the donkeys and do not find them. Saul wants to go home. The servant says a man of God is in the city. He offers his own silver as the gift, and they meet Samuel.
people.nahash.role: Ammonite king who camps against Jabesh Gilead
people.nahash.relations: Enemy of Jabesh Gilead. Saul’s army scatters his men.
people.nahash.meaning: He camps against Jabesh Gilead and demands every right eye for a covenant. The elders get seven days and send for help. Saul comes and strikes the Ammonites. Samuel later says his attack made the people ask for a king.
people.jonathan-saul.role: Saul’s son, fighter, and David’s sworn friend
people.jonathan-saul.relations: Son of Saul. Brother of Merab and Michal. He makes a covenant with David.
people.jonathan-saul.meaning: He attacks a Philistine garrison with only his armor bearer, and Israel wins. He makes a covenant with David and gives him his robe and sword. He warns David that Saul means to kill him. He dies with Saul at Mount Gilboa.
people.jonathan-armor-bearer.role: Unnamed young man who climbs with Jonathan
people.jonathan-armor-bearer.relations: He goes with Jonathan, and Saul does not know.
people.jonathan-armor-bearer.meaning: Jonathan asks him to cross to the Philistine garrison. He says he is with Jonathan. He climbs up after Jonathan and kills the men Jonathan strikes down. The two kill about twenty men, and the Philistine camp trembles.
people.ahijah-priest.role: Priest who wears an ephod with Saul
people.ahijah-priest.relations: Son of Ahitub and grandson of Phinehas, from Eli’s house.
people.ahijah-priest.meaning: He is with Saul’s six hundred men at Gibeah and wears an ephod. Saul tells him to bring God’s ark. The noise in the Philistine camp grows, and Saul tells him to stop.
people.abner.relations: Son of Ner. Ner and Saul’s father Kish are both sons of Abiel.
people.abner.meaning: He cannot tell Saul whose son David is, and he brings David in. He sits by Saul at the new moon meal. In chapter 26 he sleeps while David takes Saul’s spear. David calls out and blames him for not guarding the king.
people.ahinoam-saul.meaning: Chapter 14 names her as Saul’s wife and the daughter of Ahimaaz. She has no story in the book. She is not David’s wife Ahinoam of Jezreel.
people.merab.relations: Saul’s firstborn daughter and Michal’s sister. She is given to Adriel as wife.
people.merab.meaning: Saul offers her to David if David will fight the Philistines. Saul hopes the Philistines will kill him. When the time comes, Saul gives her to Adriel. The text records no words from her.
people.michal.relations: Saul’s younger daughter. Wife of David, later given by Saul to Palti.
people.michal.meaning: She loves David, and Saul uses that to set a trap for him. She becomes David’s wife. She lets David down through a window and lays the teraphim in his bed. Saul later gives her to Palti.
people.ishvi.role: Son named in the list of Saul’s family
people.ishvi.meaning: Chapter 14 lists him as a son of Saul with Jonathan and Malchishua. He has no story in the book. Chapter 31 names Abinadab with those two brothers and does not name Ishvi.
people.malchishua.relations: Son of Saul. Brother of Jonathan, and of Abinadab in chapter 31.
people.malchishua.meaning: Chapter 14 lists him as a son of Saul. The Philistines kill him with Jonathan and Abinadab at Mount Gilboa. The men of Jabesh Gilead take the sons’ bodies from the wall. They bury the bones.
people.agag.role: Amalekite king Saul spares and Samuel kills
people.agag.relations: Saul’s captive after the attack on Amalek.
people.agag.meaning: Saul takes him alive and spares him, against the LORD’s command. Samuel calls for him at Gilgal. Agag comes cheerfully and says the bitterness of death is past. Samuel cuts him in pieces before the LORD.
people.eliab-david.meaning: Samuel sees him first and thinks he is the LORD’s anointed. The LORD says not to look at his height. He follows Saul to battle and angrily says David came only to watch. He is not the tribal leader Eliab in Numbers.
people.abinadab-david.meaning: Jesse has him pass before Samuel, and the LORD does not choose him. He follows Saul to the battle with Eliab and Shammah. He is not the ark’s host or Saul’s son of the same name.
people.shammah.meaning: Jesse has him pass before Samuel, and the LORD does not choose him. He follows Saul to the battle with Eliab and Abinadab.
people.goliath.relations: A Philistine from Gath. David fights him alone.
people.goliath.meaning: He stands before Israel for forty days and calls for one man to fight. Saul and all Israel are afraid. David hits him in the forehead with a sling stone and cuts off his head. Later Ahimelech gives David his sword at Nob.
people.adriel.relations: Called the Meholathite. Husband of Merab.
people.adriel.meaning: Saul gives him Merab at the time she should have gone to David. The book says nothing more about him.
people.jonathan-boy.role: Unnamed boy who fetches Jonathan’s arrows
people.jonathan-boy.relations: He serves Jonathan and carries his weapons.
people.jonathan-boy.meaning: Jonathan shoots arrows and sends him to find them. Jonathan calls, “Isn’t the arrow beyond you?” That call tells David to flee. The boy knows nothing of the plan and carries the weapons to the city.
people.ahimelech-priest.role: Priest at Nob who helps David
people.ahimelech-priest.meaning: He trembles when David comes alone. He gives David holy bread and the sword of Goliath. Doeg reports it, and Saul has him and his father’s house killed. He is not Ahimelech the Hittite in chapter 26.
people.doeg.role: Saul’s Edomite herdsman who kills the priests
people.doeg.relations: An Edomite, called the best of Saul’s herdsmen.
people.doeg.meaning: He is at Nob the day Ahimelech helps David. He tells Saul what he saw. Saul’s guards will not strike the priests, so Doeg does. He kills eighty-five priests and strikes the city of Nob.
people.achish.relations: Son of Maoch. He gives David the town of Ziklag.
people.achish.meaning: David first comes to him in fear and acts insane before him. Later he takes in David and six hundred men and gives him Ziklag. He believes David’s false reports about the raids. His princes distrust David, so he sends David back before the battle.
people.gad.role: Prophet who tells David to leave the stronghold
people.gad.relations: He speaks to David while David is in the stronghold.
people.gad.meaning: He tells David not to stay in the stronghold and to go to Judah. David leaves and comes to the forest of Hereth. He is not Jacob’s son Gad or the tribe of Gad.
people.abiathar.role: Priest who escapes the killing at Nob
people.abiathar.relations: Son of Ahimelech. He joins David and brings an ephod.
people.abiathar.meaning: He escapes when Doeg kills the priests and flees to David. He tells David what Saul did, and David says to stay with him. He brings the ephod when David asks the LORD about Keilah. He brings it again at Ziklag.
people.abigail.role: Woman who stops David’s attack on Nabal
people.abigail.relations: Wife of Nabal, then wife of David.
people.abigail.meaning: A servant tells her that Nabal insulted David’s men. She loads food on donkeys, meets David, and asks him not to shed blood. David turns back, and after Nabal dies she becomes his wife. The Amalekites take her from Ziklag, and David rescues her.
people.nabal.role: Rich flock owner who refuses David’s request
people.nabal.relations: Husband of Abigail. He is of the house of Caleb.
people.nabal.meaning: David’s men protect his shepherds, then ask for food at shearing time. He insults them and gives nothing. David sets out to kill every male in his house, and Abigail stops him. Nabal hears of it, becomes like a stone, and dies about ten days later.
people.ahinoam-david.relations: Wife of David, named with Abigail. She is from Jezreel.
people.ahinoam-david.meaning: David takes her as wife in chapter 25. She lives with him at Gath and then at Ziklag. The Amalekites carry her off, and David rescues her. She is not Saul’s wife Ahinoam.
people.palti.meaning: Saul gives him Michal, though she is David’s wife. The text gives no reason and no words from Palti or Michal.
people.abishai.role: David’s companion who goes into Saul’s camp
people.abishai.meaning: He offers to go down with David into Saul’s camp at night. He asks to pin the sleeping Saul to the ground with one stroke. David says no one may strike the LORD’s anointed. They take Saul’s spear and water jar and leave.
people.ahimelech-hittite.role: Hittite man David asks about the camp visit
people.ahimelech-hittite.meaning: David asks him and Abishai who will go down to Saul’s camp. Abishai answers, and the text gives no answer from Ahimelech. He is not the priest Ahimelech of Nob.
people.endor-medium.role: Unnamed woman Saul asks to bring up Samuel
people.endor-medium.relations: Saul comes to her in disguise. She later feeds him and his servants.
people.endor-medium.meaning: Saul comes at night and asks her to bring up Samuel. She fears a trap, because Saul drove such people from the land. She cries out when she sees Samuel and knows her guest is Saul. Afterward she urges Saul to eat and cooks a calf and bread.
people.egyptian-servant.role: Sick Egyptian left behind who guides David
people.egyptian-servant.relations: Servant of an Amalekite who raided Ziklag.
people.egyptian-servant.meaning: His Amalekite master leaves him sick in the field for three days. David’s men give him bread, water, figs, and raisins. He makes David swear not to kill him or hand him back. Then he leads David to the Amalekite camp.
people.abinadab-saul.meaning: The Philistines kill him with Jonathan and Malchishua at Mount Gilboa. Chapter 14 does not list him among Saul’s sons. He is not David’s brother or the ark’s host.
people.saul-armor-bearer.role: Unnamed armor bearer at Saul’s last battle
people.saul-armor-bearer.meaning: The archers press Saul, and he asks his armor bearer to kill him. He is terrified and will not. Saul falls on his own sword, and the armor bearer does the same. He is not Jonathan’s armor bearer from chapter 14.
people.jesse.relations: Father of David and seven other sons, among them Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah.
people.jesse.meaning: He has seven sons pass before Samuel, then sends for David from the sheep. He sends David to Saul with bread, wine, and a young goat. Later he sends David to the battle with food for his brothers. David takes him to the king of Moab for safety.
people.david.role: Shepherd anointed king who flees from Saul
people.david.relations: Son of Jesse. Sworn friend of Jonathan. Husband of Michal, Abigail, and Ahinoam.
people.david.meaning: Samuel anoints him, and he plays the harp for Saul and kills Goliath. Saul tries to kill him, so he flees and gathers about six hundred men. Twice he spares Saul’s life. He lives under Achish, raids nearby peoples, leaves no one alive, and lies about it.
people.moses.meaning: Samuel says the LORD appointed Moses and Aaron. He says the LORD sent them to bring Israel’s fathers out of Egypt. Samuel uses this to show what the LORD has done for the people.
people.aaron.meaning: Samuel names him with Moses in chapter 12. He says the LORD sent the two to bring Israel’s fathers out of Egypt. Aaron has no other part in this book.
people.gideon.meaning: Samuel lists Jerubbaal among the men the LORD sent to rescue Israel. Jerubbaal is another name for Gideon. He has no other part in this book.
people.jephthah.role: Rescuer Samuel names in his speech
people.jephthah.meaning: Samuel lists him among the men the LORD sent to rescue Israel. Samuel says the LORD was already their king then. Jephthah has no other part in this book.
places.ramah.summary: Elkanah and Hannah live at Ramah in chapter 1. Samuel keeps his house and an altar there in chapter 7. The elders ask him for a king there in chapter 8. David flees to him there in chapter 19. Samuel is buried there in chapter 25.
places.ramah.limits: The marker shows a general area, not an exact spot. Chapters 9 and 10 do not name Samuel’s city.
places.shiloh.summary: Hannah prays at the LORD’s house in Shiloh in chapter 1. Samuel serves there under Eli and hears the LORD call in chapter 3. In chapter 4 the people take the ark from Shiloh to the battle. Eli dies there when he hears it is lost.
places.shiloh.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.aphek.summary: The Philistines camp at Aphek in chapter 4, then defeat Israel and take the ark. They gather their armies there again in chapter 29. There the princes make Achish send David back.
places.aphek.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.
places.ebenezer-battle.summary: Israel camps beside Ebenezer in chapter 4. The Philistines kill about four thousand men, then thirty thousand more. They take the ark and kill Hophni and Phinehas.
places.ebenezer-battle.limits: The site is not certain. Chapter 7 gives the name Ebenezer to Samuel’s stone near Mizpah.
places.ashdod.summary: The Philistines bring the ark to Ashdod in chapter 5. They set it in the house of Dagon, and Dagon falls on his face twice. Tumors strike the people, and they send the ark away.
places.ashdod.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.gath.summary: The ark comes to Gath in chapter 5, and tumors break out. Goliath comes from Gath in chapter 17. David acts insane before King Achish there in chapter 21. He lives there with six hundred men in chapter 27.
places.gath.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.ekron.summary: The ark comes to Ekron in chapter 5, and the people cry out in fear. In chapter 6 the five Philistine lords watch the ark reach Beth Shemesh. Then they return to Ekron.
places.ekron.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.beth-shemesh.summary: In chapter 6 two cows pull the ark straight to Beth Shemesh. The cart stops in the field of Joshua. The people offer the cows, and the Levites set the ark on a great stone. Many men die for looking into the ark.
places.beth-shemesh.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.kiriath-jearim.summary: The men of Beth Shemesh ask Kiriath Jearim to take the ark in chapter 6. In chapter 7 the ark goes to Abinadab’s house on the hill. His son Eleazar keeps it, and it stays twenty years.
places.kiriath-jearim.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.mizpah.summary: Samuel gathers Israel at Mizpah in chapter 7. The people fast, and the LORD thunders against the Philistines. In chapter 10 Samuel calls the tribes there, and the lot falls on Saul. Saul is found hiding among the baggage.
places.mizpah.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. Mizpeh of Moab in chapter 22 is a different place.
places.bethel.summary: Samuel visits Bethel each year in chapter 7. He judges Israel there, at Gilgal, and at Mizpah.
places.bethel.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.gilgal.summary: Samuel judges at Gilgal each year in chapter 7. The people make Saul king there in chapter 11. Saul offers the burnt offering there in chapter 13 before Samuel comes. In chapter 15 Samuel tells Saul he is rejected and kills Agag there.
places.gilgal.limits: The site is not certain. Chapter 12 follows the Gilgal gathering but does not name its place.
places.beersheba.summary: Samuel’s sons Joel and Abijah are judges in Beersheba in chapter 8. They take bribes there, and the elders ask for a king.
places.beersheba.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.gibeah.summary: Saul goes home to Gibeah in chapter 10. Messengers from Jabesh find him there in chapter 11. He waits there with six hundred men in chapter 14. In chapter 22 he sits there and orders the priests killed.
places.gibeah.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. Chapters 16 and 18 to 20 show Saul’s house but do not name the town.
places.jabesh-gilead.summary: Nahash the Ammonite camps against Jabesh Gilead in chapter 11, and Saul rescues the town. In chapter 31 its men walk all night to Beth Shan. They bring back the bodies of Saul and his sons and bury the bones.
places.jabesh-gilead.limits: The marker shows a general area, not an exact spot.
places.michmash.summary: Saul keeps two thousand men at Michmash in chapter 13. Then the Philistines camp there with a great army. In chapter 14 Jonathan and his armor bearer climb to their garrison near Michmash. Israel strikes the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon.
places.michmash.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.carmel-judah.summary: Saul sets up a monument for himself at Carmel in chapter 15. Nabal shears his sheep there in chapter 25. David’s men ask him for food there, and Abigail later leaves Carmel to marry David.
places.carmel-judah.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location. This is not Mount Carmel in the north.
places.bethlehem.summary: Samuel comes to Bethlehem in chapter 16 and anoints David among his brothers. In chapter 17 David feeds his father’s sheep there. Jesse sends him from there to the battle with food.
places.bethlehem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.elah.summary: Saul and Israel camp in the valley of Elah in chapter 17. Goliath calls for a fighter for forty days. David kills him there with a sling and a stone.
places.elah.limits: The marker shows the valley’s general area. The exact camps are not known.
places.nob.summary: David comes to Ahimelech the priest at Nob in chapter 21. He gets holy bread and the sword of Goliath, and Doeg sees it. In chapter 22 Doeg kills eighty-five priests and strikes the city. Abiathar escapes.
places.nob.limits: The site is not certain. The marker shows a general area.
places.adullam.summary: David escapes to Adullam’s cave in chapter 22. His brothers and his father’s house come to him. About four hundred men in distress or debt gather to him there.
places.adullam.limits: The marker shows a general area. It does not mark the cave.
places.moab.summary: David goes to Mizpeh of Moab in chapter 22. He asks the king of Moab to shelter his father and mother. They stay with the king while David is in the stronghold.
places.moab.limits: The marker stands for a wide region. The text does not locate Mizpeh of Moab.
places.keilah.summary: David saves Keilah from the Philistines in chapter 23. Saul plans to trap him inside its gates. The LORD tells David that the men of Keilah will hand him over. David leaves with about six hundred men.
places.keilah.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.
places.ziph.summary: David hides in the wilderness of Ziph in chapter 23, and Jonathan visits him there. The Ziphites tell Saul where he is. They tell Saul again in chapter 26. There David takes Saul’s spear and water jar at night.
places.ziph.limits: The marker stands for a wide wilderness area. The hill of Hachilah is not located.
places.maon.summary: Saul nearly surrounds David in the wilderness of Maon in chapter 23. A messenger calls Saul away to fight the Philistines. In chapter 25 Nabal is a man of Maon with flocks in Carmel.
places.maon.limits: The marker shows a general area, not an exact spot.
places.en-gedi.summary: David lives in the strongholds of En Gedi. In chapter 24 Saul brings three thousand men and enters a cave there. David cuts off the skirt of Saul’s robe and lets him live.
places.en-gedi.limits: The marker shows the general location. It does not mark the cave.
places.ziklag.summary: Achish gives Ziklag to David in chapter 27, and David raids from there. In chapter 30 the Amalekites burn Ziklag and carry off the families. David wins everyone back. He sends plunder from Ziklag to the elders of Judah.
places.ziklag.limits: The site is not certain. Chapter 29 sends David back to his place without naming Ziklag.
places.shunem.summary: The Philistines camp at Shunem in chapter 28. Saul sees their army from Gilboa and is afraid.
places.shunem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.gilboa.summary: Saul gathers Israel and camps at Gilboa in chapter 28. In chapter 31 the Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa. Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua are killed, and Saul falls on his sword.
places.gilboa.limits: The marker stands for the whole mountain. The battle spot is not known.
places.endor.summary: Saul’s servants tell him of a woman at Endor in chapter 28. Saul goes to her by night in disguise. She brings up Samuel, who says Saul and his sons will die tomorrow. She feeds Saul before he leaves.
places.endor.limits: The marker shows a general area, not an exact spot.
places.jezreel.summary: The Israelites camp by the spring in Jezreel in chapter 29. The Philistines send David away and then go up to Jezreel.
places.jezreel.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location. It does not mark the spring.
places.besor.summary: Two hundred of David’s men are too faint to cross the brook Besor (chapter 30). David goes on with four hundred and defeats the Amalekites. Back at the brook he rules that both groups share the plunder alike.
places.besor.limits: The marker stands for a wide stream area. The crossing place is not known.
places.beth-shan.summary: The Philistines fasten Saul’s body to the wall of Beth Shan in chapter 31. The men of Jabesh Gilead come by night. They take down the bodies of Saul and his sons.
places.beth-shan.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
sources.web.limits: The text tells the story. It cannot prove its own dates, battle deaths, reign lengths, or how people looked.
sources.atlas.summary: This Church-published atlas shows the wider setting. It marks some disputed places.
sources.atlas.limits: Use the place labels as background. The linked atlas also includes Latter-day Saint commentary.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: Map positions are estimates for display. A town marker does not prove any event there.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain helps show the land. It does not show ancient shorelines or towns.
sources.yale-samuel.summary: Hayes studies Samuel’s leadership and the book’s differing views of kings. She also studies how the story’s view of Saul and David changes.
sources.yale-samuel.limits: The published transcript sections that begin at 23:05 and 32:46 were reviewed. Audio and video were not checked. The transcript sometimes says Judges where it means 1 Samuel. It sometimes names Samuel where it means Saul. This guide follows the Bible text.
sources.scholar-mccarter.summary: The publisher describes McCarter’s work on how Samuel’s text was passed down. It also names the book’s written sources, language, and ancient setting.
sources.dm-samuel.summary: McClellan argues that elohim is not a word for human judges. His discussion includes the translation of 1 Samuel 2:25.
sources.dm-samuel.limits: Only the translation discussion in the original post is used. This is one scholar’s older argument. This guide leaves out its personal criticisms. It does not claim that scholars agree.
sources.net-saul-reign.summary: The translation notes describe missing or disputed numbers for Saul’s reign. They also describe proposed fixes that remain uncertain.
sources.net-saul-reign.limits: Published notes 1–2 were reviewed. Proposed numbers do not fix exact dates. Manuscripts were not inspected.
sources.lds-samuel-early.summary: The older manual studies Hannah, Samuel’s call, the ark, the kingship, and Saul’s actions.
sources.lds-samuel-early.limits: The relevant 1980 commentary sections were reviewed. Its older history claims about disease, metalwork, and ancient beliefs were not checked here.
sources.lds-samuel-late.summary: The older manual studies David’s choosing, flight, and restraint. It also studies Abigail’s plea and Saul’s visit to Endor.
sources.lds-samuel-late.limits: Church teaching is kept apart from the Bible text and from history checks.
sources.cfm-2026-23.summary: The lesson studies prayer in hardship and Samuel’s call. It also studies faithful living, which matters more than holding the ark.
sources.cfm-2026-23.limits: This is Church teaching and application. It does not prove event dates or archaeological finds.
sources.cfm-2026-24.summary: The lesson studies Christ as King, calls to serve, and obedience. It also studies judging a person by more than looks.
sources.cfm-2026-24.limits: This is Church teaching and application. It does not prove event dates or archaeological finds.
sources.cfm-2026-25.summary: The lesson studies courage, friendship, self-control, and forgiveness. It compares Abigail’s plea to David with Jesus Christ.
sources.cfm-2026-25.limits: This is Church teaching and application. It does not prove event dates or archaeological finds.
sources.wiki-1-samuel.summary: The Samuel books tell of the prophet’s childhood and the ark. They go on to Saul’s rule and David’s rise. This background covers both books.
sources.wiki-1-samuel.limits: Anyone can edit this source. Use it for background and to find other sources. Its disputed history claims need separate review by scholars.
sources.met-555866.limits: It is an Egyptian comparison, not David’s harp. Its surviving parts cannot show how Bible songs sounded.
